messages.content: What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?

message.content: Lion (*Panthera leo*) and zebra (*Equus quagga*) belong to different families within the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla respectively—so they diverged very early on after mammals split into separate lineages. Their most recent common ancestor would have been a primitive mammal living around **200–250 million years ago** during the late Triassic‑early Jurassic period when the first true mammals appeared. This ancestral species was small, insectivorous, and likely had simple dentition compared with modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates.
